Formulation  
Patient presents with acute onset of diarrhea, vomiting, abdominal pain localized to periumbilical area, and fever suggestive of infectious gastroenteritis, likely viral given family and community outbreak context. Inability to retain fluids raises concern for dehydration. Predisposing factors are minimal; precipitating factor likely recent exposure to an infectious agent via close contact with affected brother. Perpetuating factors include ongoing vomiting limiting oral rehydration effectiveness. Protective factors include patient awareness, family support, and ability to pass urine indicating some hydration.

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Acute infectious gastroenteritis with dehydration risk  
- Patient Goal(s): Remain hydrated, reduce vomiting and diarrhea symptoms, recover to resume normal activities including work  
- Clinical Goal(s): Ensure hydration status remains stable, identify causative agent via stool sample, initiate appropriate treatment if bacterial infection present  
- Actions (Patient): Continue oral rehydration salts in small frequent sips, avoid foods that exacerbate symptoms, attend urgent clinic appointment for assessment and stool sample collection, monitor for worsening symptoms  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Arrange urgent clinic appointment for hydration assessment and stool testing, provide instructions on home care including fluid intake and dietary advice, advise emergency department attendance if symptoms worsen, follow-up after sample results  

Secondary Problem: Not recorded  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Importance of hydration, use of oral rehydration salts, dietary modifications, recognition of worsening symptoms requiring emergency care  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Inability to retain any fluids, increased weakness, decreased urine output, high fever, bloody stools, severe abdominal pain  
- Coping Strategies: Use of simple dietary measures, small frequent fluid intake, prompt reporting of symptom progression
